newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian child murder investigators visit Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Belgian child murder investigators visit Ireland.

text.p: Police investigating the child abduction, rape and murder scandals that have rocked Belgium for the past nine months will visit Ireland to get more information, the lawyer for the wife of the chief suspect said on Friday.

The lawyer for Michelle Martin, the wife of convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, told reporters the visit would be in connection with the disappearance in August 1995 of teenagers An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks, Belga news agency reported.
Their bodies were found in early September last year, buried under a shed on a property connected with Dutroux in the central city of Charleroi.
Dutroux and accomplice Michel Lelievre abducted and drugged the two girls as they were hitching back to their holiday lodgings in the port of Ostend.
But the two men's car broke down on the way south and Dutroux himself hitched a lift with an Irish couple back to his house in Sars-La-Buissiere to pick up another vehicle.
Martin, in jail along with Dutroux and two other men connected with the killings, noted the Irish couple's car registration and has given it to police. Dutroux has been charged with murder.
A total of five children have so far been found dead in Belgium since last August.

The bodies of eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo, who disappeared in June 1995, were found 14 months later buried in the garden of Dutroux' Sars-la-Buissiere home -- one of six he owns in the Charleroi region.

The body of eight-year-old Loubna Benaissa, who went missing in Brussels in August 1992 while on a local shopping trip, was found last month in a steel trunk in the cellar of a local garage. Convicted child molester Patrick Derochette has been charged with abduction and rape leading to the death of a minor.
